schema: revision-roadmap machine transcription (legacy v1.0 re-review input)

items.title: Interpretive anchor for the skill increment
items.verification_criteria: Give the skill increment an interpretive anchor and bridge it to the standardised and population-level percentage contrasts
items.evidence_anchor: text: Introduction "in one US health system, adding neighbourhood variables to a clinical model predicting advanced prostate cancer changed the AUC from 0.671 to 0.673"

items.title: Replace the AUC example
items.verification_criteria: Replace the AUC 0.671 to 0.673 example with an argument that small gains are informative
items.evidence_anchor: text: Introduction "in one US health system, adding neighbourhood variables to a clinical model predicting advanced prostate cancer changed the AUC from 0.671 to 0.673"

items.title: Low-risk share with its denominator
items.verification_criteria: Report the low-risk share (82%, 98%) alongside the absolute step 2 skill wherever it appears
items.evidence_anchor: table: Table 2, low risk rows — social position as 82 and 98 percent of step 2 skill, where step 2 skill is 0.76 and 0.99

items.title: Direction stated for the joint area contrast only
items.verification_criteria: State direction only for the joint area contrast; remove separate rural and lower-income directions from the Conclusions and Discussion
items.reviewer: EIC, R1, R3 (CONSENSUS-3; R2 silent); DA
items.evidence_anchor: text: Conclusions "the social signal is small and consistent, and points to less delay, not more, in rural and lower-income counties"

items.title: Concentration-index caveat restored
items.verification_criteria: Restore the caveat that the income concentration index does not separate income from rurality and is not standardised for clinical features
items.reviewer: EIC, R1, R3 (CONSENSUS-3; R2 silent); DA
items.evidence_anchor: text: Abstract, Results "delay was concentrated among men in higher-income counties (Erreygers index 0.062, 0.039 to 0.083; 0 means no income gradient)"

items.title: Title names the estimand
items.verification_criteria: Retitle so the title names the social-position increment, and shorten it
items.evidence_anchor: text: Title "how much is clinical need?"

items.title: Australian material placed as context
items.verification_criteria: Move Australian and Tasmanian material (including the two lung cancer studies) into a labelled context or transferability paragraph; resolve the "different directions" tension
items.evidence_anchor: text: Title "how much is clinical need?" [EIC W3 anchor; R2 W3 anchor: text: Introduction "These studies report adjusted associations for one factor at a time, usually pooled across risk groups."]

items.title: 90-day threshold rationale for US data
items.verification_criteria: Give a 90-day threshold rationale that stands on its own for US data (cite [8]) and state that the SEER interval is not the pathway's measure
items.evidence_anchor: text: Methods, Outcome "a wait of more than 90 days, following the optimal care pathway benchmark"

items.title: Verifiable protocol timing
items.verification_criteria: Make protocol timing verifiable: public timestamped protocol and commit identifiers or times in the amendment log (S32)
items.evidence_anchor: text: Methods, Protocol "It was committed to version control before the first cohort was built; it was not registered externally"

items.title: Code repository link
items.verification_criteria: Supply a public, timestamped code repository link
items.evidence_anchor: text: Reporting checklists "IN PREPARATION: STROBE, RECORD and TRIPOD+AI checklists with page references."

items.title: Reporting checklists
items.verification_criteria: Complete STROBE, RECORD and TRIPOD+AI checklists with section references and address missing items
items.evidence_anchor: absence: Supplement, Reporting checklists — expected completed STROBE, RECORD and TRIPOD+AI checklists with section references; checked Methods (Reporting and ethics), Declarations, the final supplement section

items.title: Declarations
items.verification_criteria: Complete all declarations (affiliation, ethics, funding, competing interests, AI-use disclosure)
items.evidence_anchor: text: Declarations, Use of AI tools "[TO BE COMPLETED: disclosure statement]"

items.title: Leave-one-variable-out range
items.verification_criteria: Correct the leave-one-variable-out range to 0.18 to 0.45
items.reviewer: EIC, R1, R2 (CONSENSUS-3; R3 silent); DA
items.evidence_anchor: table: Supplementary Table S8 — intermediate risk, penalised logistic regression, marital status 0.18 and rurality 0.19

items.title: High-risk standardised difference
items.verification_criteria: Correct the high-risk "under 3 points" statement (pooled contrast under 3 points; high-risk models disagreed)
items.evidence_anchor: text: Discussion, The rural direction "although the standardised difference was under 3 points"

items.title: "Models disagree" label
items.verification_criteria: Replace the "models disagree" label with one that describes same-direction, below-threshold cases
items.evidence_anchor: table: Table 3 — low risk, marital status 3.6 and 2.4 labelled "models disagree"

items.title: Secondary-outcome grid-edge disclosure
items.verification_criteria: Report secondary-outcome C values and the grid-edge limitation
items.evidence_anchor: absence: Results (Secondary outcome) and Limitations — expected a statement that logistic regression chose C at a grid edge in intermediate and high risk for the secondary outcome, as in reports/phase4_receipt.md; checked Methods (Secondary outcome), Results (Secondary outcome), Limitations, Supplementary Tables S25 to S31

items.title: Prose exposition and shorter abstract
items.verification_criteria: Rewrite Introduction and Discussion as prose; shorten the abstract
items.evidence_anchor: text: Abstract, Results (nested bullets) "Social position increment"

items.title: Strengths wording on uncertainty
items.verification_criteria: Reword the Strengths claim about county-level uncertainty to describe the cell-level cluster bootstrap proxy
items.evidence_anchor: text: Discussion, Strengths "Uncertainty that respects county-level exposures"

items.title: Figure scales
items.verification_criteria: Common or captioned x-axis scales in Figure 3; revise Figure 4b; note the truncated axis in Figure 4a
items.evidence_anchor: figure: Figure 3 — panel x-axis ranges 0 to 4, 0 to 2 and 0 to 1

items.title: Income band labelling
items.verification_criteria: Rename income "quartile of 16 bands" groups and give dollar ranges
items.evidence_anchor: table: Table 1 — County median household income (quartile of 16 bands), Q1 8.0% and Q4 32.8% of men

items.title: Accurate description of prior work and hedged novelty
items.verification_criteria: Describe prior models accurately (multivariable, not one factor at a time), describe how prior work was identified, and hedge the novelty claim to the search done
items.evidence_anchor: text: Introduction "These studies report adjusted associations for one factor at a time, usually pooled across risk groups."

items.title: Closest precedents cited and positioned
items.verification_criteria: Cite and position the closest precedents (Stokes 2013, Ajjawi 2026, Semprini 2026, Baade 2012; [11] as incremental-value precedent)
items.evidence_anchor: absence: Introduction references — expected Stokes 2013, Ajjawi 2026, Semprini 2026 and Baade 2012 cited and set apart; checked Introduction, Discussion, reference list [R2 W3 missing references]

items.title: Model-fitting and cross-fitting uncertainty in headline intervals
items.verification_criteria: Propagate model-fitting and cross-fitting uncertainty into the primary-estimand intervals (minimum: repeat cross-fitting over several fold seeds and report the spread)
items.evidence_anchor: text: Methods, Models and validation, Uncertainty "500 resamples of out-of-fold predictions, percentile intervals, no refitting"

items.title: Bootstrap clustering unit and cell sizes
items.verification_criteria: Report bootstrap cell count and size distribution per stratum; justify cells as the dependence unit or add an alternative-clustering sensitivity analysis
items.evidence_anchor: table: Table 1 — large metropolitan counties 194,681 men [R1 W1 locator; finding anchor shared with R17: Methods, Uncertainty]

items.title: Per-step tuning
items.verification_criteria: Tune hyperparameters separately at each step (at least steps 1 and 2); report resulting LightGBM increments and limit the model-comparison inference to strata where the flexible clinical model is at least as good
items.evidence_anchor: table: Supplementary Table S7, low risk, LightGBM, step 1 log-loss skill 0.02 and calibration slope 0.883 against penalised logistic regression 0.14 and 0.998

items.title: One-at-a-time profile table
items.verification_criteria: Publish the one-at-a-time rurality and income profile table promised by amendment 1.7, with the model disagreement stated
items.evidence_anchor: text: Supplementary Table S32, amendment version 1.7 "with the one-at-a-time results kept in a supplementary table"

items.title: Post hoc labels for agreement rule and dropped intervals
items.verification_criteria: Label the 3-point agreement rule and the dropped intervals as post hoc in Methods and the abstract; state that area and marital differences lack uncertainty measures
items.evidence_anchor: text: Supplementary Table S32, amendment 1.7 "Prompted by the model disagreement seen in the development run"

items.title: Year-aware concentration index
items.verification_criteria: Report county income rank distribution by diagnosis year and add a year-stratified or year-standardised concentration index
items.evidence_anchor: absence: Methods and Results, Income inequality — expected an index stratified or standardised by year of diagnosis, or a report of how county income band varies with diagnosis year; checked Methods Income inequality, Results Income inequality, Figure 4b legend, Supplementary Table S12, Limitations

items.title: Weighting precision claim
items.verification_criteria: Report weighted and unweighted percentages at a precision that supports "0.2 points or less", or restate the claim
items.evidence_anchor: text: Results, Which social variable "Removing marital status or rurality each lost 0.22 to 0.45 points in the pooled, intermediate- and high-risk strata" [R1 W5 anchor; weighting sub-claim in same finding]

items.title: TRIPOD+AI prediction-model items
items.verification_criteria: Add TRIPOD+AI prediction-model items: LightGBM missing-value handling, interaction terms, model availability, subgroup performance, cluster count
items.evidence_anchor: text: Reporting checklists "IN PREPARATION: STROBE, RECORD and TRIPOD+AI checklists with page references."

items.title: Model-comparison uncertainty caveat
items.verification_criteria: Add the caveat that no interval was computed for the LightGBM versus logistic difference
items.evidence_anchor: text: Abstract, Results "LightGBM had higher out-of-fold skill than penalised logistic regression in every risk group."

items.title: Year specification in logistic base model
items.verification_criteria: Enter year as categories or a spline in the logistic base model and report the logistic increment
items.evidence_anchor: text: Methods, Ordered feature steps "year of diagnosis and a 2020 indicator"

items.title: Conditioning on recorded curative treatment
items.verification_criteria: State the conditioning on recorded curative treatment in the abstract and Conclusions; carry "not evidence of better care" forward; say the bounds do not cover selection into the treated cohort and discuss bias direction for area measures
items.evidence_anchor: text: Conclusions "points to less delay, not more, in rural and lower-income counties" [R3 W2 anchor, full Conclusions sentence]

items.title: "98 of 100" wording
items.verification_criteria: State that 98 of 100 refers to intervals, and note the 0.00 lower bound
items.evidence_anchor: text: Abstract "stayed above 0 in 98 of 100 results" [R1 Minor Issues; DA minor list]

items.title: Hormone therapy and the triage reading
items.verification_criteria: Qualify the "triage" reading: state that higher-risk radiotherapy patients often start hormone therapy first; bring the prostatectomy-only gradient into the main text; report the clinical-need increment for that scenario
items.evidence_anchor: table: Supplementary Table S19, primary analysis row against the radical prostatectomy without radiotherapy only row — low risk 47.9 against 45.8, high risk 32.8 against 38.4

items.title: Risk-group construction described accurately
items.verification_criteria: Correct the "clinical information only" risk-group sentence; state that regional stage is often pathological for surgical men; consider a step 1 sensitivity analysis without stage
items.evidence_anchor: text: Methods, Clinical risk groups "Risk groups used clinical information only, because pathological grade is observed only after surgery."

items.title: "Lower is better" labels
items.verification_criteria: Remove or qualify "lower is better" labels, especially for low-risk men; state once that a longer wait is not necessarily worse care
items.evidence_anchor: text: Abstract, Results "39.7% waited more than 90 days (lower is better)"

items.title: Low-risk narrow-stratum wording
items.verification_criteria: Say "recorded clinical variables, which vary little within this group by definition" for the low-risk comparison
items.evidence_anchor: text: Abstract, Results "in low-risk men it added more than clinical need did."

items.title: Active-surveillance exclusion as assumption
items.verification_criteria: Present the active-surveillance exclusion as an assumption; cite the coding rule; report the share of intervals over 365 days and top-coded, by risk group
items.evidence_anchor: text: Methods, Active surveillance "Men whose first course was active surveillance have surgery and radiation coded as none, so they are not in this cohort."

items.title: Huang et al. [22] scope
items.verification_criteria: Restrict the Huang et al. [22] claim to favourable-risk disease; use its rural surveillance finding in the selection discussion
items.evidence_anchor: text: Discussion, Marital status "This is consistent with higher use of surveillance or watchful waiting among unmarried men in an earlier SEER study [22]."

items.title: Noone 80% context
items.verification_criteria: Give the scope of Noone's 80% figure and carry its caution into the secondary-outcome interpretation
items.evidence_anchor: text: Limitations "Against Medicare claims, SEER identified radiation therapy with 80% sensitivity [20]."

items.title: Area-measure equivalence wording
items.verification_criteria: Replace "corresponds to" with candidate-analogue wording in Supplementary Box 2; avoid "remote" for US counties
items.evidence_anchor: text: Supplementary Box 2 "the Rural-Urban Continuum Code corresponds to Australian Statistical Geography Standard remoteness areas, assigned by residential postcode."

items.title: Ang et al. [10] attribution
items.verification_criteria: Attribute the waiting-time paradox to [10] and the triage explanation to the authors or a prostate-specific source
items.evidence_anchor: text: Introduction "Men with aggressive disease are treated sooner, which is why unadjusted comparisons of waiting time and survival can run in the wrong direction [10]."

items.title: Large centres and time-trend literature
items.verification_criteria: Set the metropolitan direction and the 2010 to 2022 rise against evidence on large centres and time trends (e.g. Khorana 2019)
items.evidence_anchor: text: Discussion, The rural direction "The data cannot test explanations such as longer surgical queues in large centres, second opinions, or wider choice of treatment settings."

items.title: SEER Gleason and PSA variable names
items.verification_criteria: Name the SEER variables for clinical Gleason score and PSA in the manuscript
items.evidence_anchor: absence: Methods and Declarations — expected completed STROBE and RECORD checklists, an ethics statement, SEER variable names for clinical Gleason score and PSA, and a code repository link; checked Methods, Declarations, Reporting checklists section, Supplementary material

items.title: The "social position" label
items.verification_criteria: Rename or qualify "social position" in the title, abstract and Conclusions; state prominently that two of three variables are ecological and that registry differences load onto the block
items.evidence_anchor: text: Methods, Uncertainty "The social block is interpreted as geographic and social position, including any unmeasured registry differences"

items.title: Excess waiting days metric
items.verification_criteria: Report excess waiting days per man, the top-coded share, and why the 7-day threshold could not be applied
items.evidence_anchor: table: Supplementary Table S11, all men — 30,597 and 20,014 crude excess days per 1,000 men

items.title: Foley 2025 population restriction
items.verification_criteria: Restore the Foley 2025 restriction (men not treated with external beam radiotherapy) in the Discussion
items.evidence_anchor: text: Discussion, What an Australian registry could add "They reported an adjusted difference of 9.25 days by remoteness, and of 42 to 59 days between public and private facilities"

items.title: Concentration-index tie rule and need standardisation
items.verification_criteria: State the fractional-rank tie rule and whether delay was need-standardised for the concentration index
items.evidence_anchor: absence: Methods, Income inequality — expected the fractional-rank rule for men tied within county income bands and whether delay was need-standardised; checked Methods Income inequality, Supplementary Table S12, Figure 4 legend

items.title: Sensitivity agreement is not independent replication
items.verification_criteria: State that sensitivity scenarios reuse largely the same men, so agreement is not independent replication
items.evidence_anchor: text: Discussion "consistent across ... ten sensitivity analyses" [DA minor list locator]

items.title: Comparability of the SEER diagnosis date as start point
items.verification_criteria: Address whether the SEER diagnosis date is a comparable start point across registries, years and settings (raised as a question, not an established defect)
items.evidence_anchor: absence: Discussion — expected discussion of start-date recording consistency; checked per DA Unexamined premise
